answer: An agent network limits Sybil attacks by tying node identities to line-of-sight laser transceivers. Nodes authenticate by exchanging synchronized optical pulses between a coastal wharf, a canyon relay, and an elevated ledge. Attackers incur substantial hardware and geographic deployment costs per physical transceiver instead of spawning virtual clones. However, atmospheric fog and dust attenuate optical beams, intermittently interrupting verification for honest agents.
